Surveying monocycle robot GMC-69 with multipurpose prospecting functions.  Vatrushka's complex system of cameras and sensors is capable of high-precision tachymetric surveying.  Thanks to the built-in seismograph, Vatrushka can detect mineral deposits, solve hydrogeological and geotechnical problems, and carry out seismic microzoning.

The large-scale surveyor robot HOG-7 collects rare plants and minerals.  Despite its impressive size, Hedgie can switch to the Tumbleweed mode, accelerating and retracting its long limbs to reach speeds of up to 50 km/h.  Hedgie's limbs feature special drills and a compressor that can easily pick up valuable resources from the Earth's surface. Thanks to detailed cartographical data stored on an in-built hard drive, Hedgie can gather and instantly analyze available topographic and geodetic materials. The HOG-8 model will be equipped with state-of-the-art wireless transmission technology.

The large MA-9 robot is used for construction and welding work.   Belyash can easily carry a load of half a ton. Its average service life amounts to at least 20 years. Unlike the MA-7 and MA-8 that did manual or semi-automatic welding, MA-9 is equipped with the argon-arc welding technology. It is expected that MA-10 will finally feature laser welding.  Thanks to its steel-titanium alloy shell, Belyash can operate even in extreme conditions, at ambient temperatures between -75 and +75 °C. Its chassis is based on a chimpanzee skeleton, and MA-9 can climb steep surfaces and construction beams just like its prototype. Comrade Abalakov, a renowned mountain climber, took part in the development of Belyash's hands.

The rotation speed of the mower blades starts at 540 rpm.  Use extreme caution when switching it on to prevent accidents.

The MFU-68 robot was designed for the needs of animal husbandry and serves as a shepherd for cows, sheep, goats, and so on.  The Laborer traverses rough terrain with ease and is immune to the harsh weather conditions of the Far North or Mongolian steppes. To control a large herd, Laborers can join into groups.  The MFU-68/L variation is an improved model of the Laborer equipped with a 40-cm circular blade for felling trees at logging sites. The Laborer shows good results when paired with the MTU-7 Bumblebee log transporter. It is resistant to weather conditions and can withstand temperatures as low as -45 °C.

The little Sprout is a link between the worlds of botany and zoology and the future of food production.  Featuring a mixture of plant and animal proteins, it is the unprocessed food of the future. Cultivating Sprouts is a humane alternative to animal husbandry: no longer will millions of cows and chickens have to be slaughtered on a daily basis to feed Soviet citizens. Better yet, Sprouts can move about independently: healthy food will find its way to the hungry on its own!

The WSP-9 light transport drone performs deliveries and can repair any technical object, including other robots connected to the Kollektiv ecosystem.  Pchela has increased maneuverability and high speed of flight due to its small size, but cannot lift loads heavier than 25 kg.  Pchela repairs objects using a flexible cable that can be secured in any position and holds the Polymer arc welding wire.

The RAF-9 robot can produce, operate, and maintain various kinds of equipment.  The Engineer can operate basic metal-cutting, woodworking, and stone-cutting machinery as well as complex computerized devices. All Engineer models feature protocols for optimal repair of simple non-robotic equipment.  Engineers are used not only in production but also in everyday life: the robot can easily work as a janitor, electrician, locksmith, or plumber, freeing its owners from the drudgery of daily chores.

The medium universal copter MUC-1 is mainly used to transport cargo over short distances.  Drofa easily reaches speeds of up to 50 km/h and can carry loads of several hundred kilograms.  In addition to cargo transportation, Drofa is used in the agricultural industry. Thanks to the unique shape of the blades which operate on the principle of the Archimedes screw, it can transport water for remote field and pasture irrigation.

The TER/A1 robot performs basic administrative and advisory functions.  This anthropomorphic robotic assistant is based on the VOV/A6 and designed with the participation of Comrade Tereshkova, the actress, cosmonaut, and decorated Soviet hero. The TER/A1 robot is the most advanced product of Facility 3826, addressing the shortcomings of the previous generation and introducing many new features such as voice modulation and self-repair.  Tereshkova is one of the few robots independent from the Kollektiv ecosystem: it still reacts only to verbal human commands. Perhaps after the launch of Kollektiv everyone will be able to enjoy a virtual Tereshkova of their own.

The VOV-A6 robot helps scientists carry out experiments and tests in research facilities.  The Lab Tech was given human shape to prevent negative psychological effects on human employees. Originally, the Lab Tech shell was made of aluminum alloys and plastic, but after the groundbreaking biological Polymer discovery all latest models are shipped in a cutting-edge lifelike hull.  Its anthropomorphic hand prostheses have over 100 sensors, providing the high precision required in handling hazardous substances.

The flying Mutant is the surprise result of symbiosis between a Sprout and a human corpse.  When a Sprout finds a dead body, it grows its stems through the mouth and nose, penetrating the brain and taking control of the corpse's motor functions in under a minute. The hybrid is fully submissive to the Sprout and can either move on two legs or hover on propeller-like leaves.

The scary Plyusch is the endoskeleton of an experimental bionic creature, consisting of an animated blob of polymeric muscles with an implanted dog brain.   The Plyusch usually moves on its hind legs, but can run on all fours at the speed of a wild wolf. The biorobot can extend its limbs to several times their original length and jump dozens of meters high.

The heavy-duty land robot loader NA-T256 carries weights up to 2.5 tons and is used for complex repair works.  Natasha is widely used on construction sites all over the USSR. The enormous engine power and battery capacity allows up to 24 hours of continuous operation on a single battery charge. Without Natasha the construction of Dneprovskaya, Kuibyshevskaya, and Stalingradskaya hydroelectric power plants would have been impossible, not to mention finishing the Baikonur Cosmodrome ahead of schedule.  Some of the Natasha models are equipped with adjusted rocket engines, developed under the guidance of Comrade Korolev, which allow the heavy robot to climb to proportionate heights, assuming the safety precautions are observed: no people without protection gear can be near Natasha during the take off.

The many-limbed Dewdrop is a heavy bionic creature, a massive blob of biological Polymer muscle, wrapped in synthetic membrane that both helps the robot to maintain shape and facilitates transportation on an industrial scale.  The biorobot will be used in the mining industry: not only can it lift heavy loads, it also performs precise borehole drilling with its mechanical laser unit.

The MED-6 medical robot can replace a nurse and perform different procedures from drawing blood to carrying out diagnostic surgeries.   The Medic is based on the MFU-68 Laborer chassis. The main difference between the two are the Medic's larger legs, which are required to treat patients both on the floor and in hospital beds. The Medic's head unit is equipped with a multifunctional appliance for routine medical operations such as blood sampling.  Its replaceable tanks contain various biological Polymer solutions, such as anesthetic and antiseptic liquids.

The light universal copter LUC-1 performs various tasks in the agro-industrial and livestock complex, watching the crops and pastures in the Soviet collective farms.  Unlike the larger Drofa model, the Owl is smaller and has lower lifting power, but makes up for it by featuring better mobility: Owls can reach speeds of up to 75 km/h. Several Owls can team up to transport heavy loads.  The main purpose of the Owl is to keep a watchful eye on cattle.

Alexey Lebedev is an electrical engineer and energy specialist and the founder of Soviet computing technology. He was the head of the All-Russian Electronics Institute's automation department and the director of the Institute of Precision Mechanics and Computing Technology. Lebedev created the first electronic analog computing machine in the country in order to solve ordinary differential equations that are frequently encountered in energy-related fields. The first small electronic calculation machine in the Soviet Union and Continental Europe was also developed under his leadership. He is the head of a top-secret AoC department, but, thanks to his friend and colleague Privalov, he has been able to free himself from administrative duties and continue studying the quantum entanglement of radio waves. The Radio of the Future is his most cherished and inimitable creation.

Although he has no interest whatsoever in the theater, Papkin knows robots and complex technological processes like the back of his hand. An introvert, he prefers to work at night in order to avoid his coworkers. He is a heavy smoker, which has led to a great deal of conflict with the performers, who often complain about the acrid stench of his cheap tobacco.

Dr. Sechenov is a neurosurgeon, roboticist, inventor, and philanthropist. He began his career studying collective intelligence at the Soviet Academy of Medical Sciences' Brain Research Center, where he hoped to engineer a perfect way of life for the communal cities of the future. He worked on the ManKind Project before the war, but dedicated himself to studying the Polymer after it was discovered. After World War II he was put in charge of a robotics program designed to make up for the country's significant lack of human resources and took over Facility 3826 on Comrade Stalin's personal order. Once Soviet robots had been distributed throughout the world, Comrade Sechenov become the Minister of Industry. His revolutionary discovery of the Polymer's capacity for mimetic adaption made it possible to inject this extraordinarily promising new technology into human tissues. This laid the framework for what would later become Kollektiv 2.0, a merging of humans and machines into a single neural network capable of fundamentally transforming and improving the everyday lives of not just Soviet citizens, but the entire world.

Despite his parents' and teachers' expectations, Petelka did not become a famous physicist. Although he certainly had the potential, the young man's exceptional mind and fantastic imagination ultimately allowed his reach to exceed his grasp. Comrade Petelka learned about robots from a newspaper article even before the war and never stopped fantasizing about them. Petelka did end up becoming a physicist, although he was never famous. He worked with Comrade Filimonenko on a cold Polymer synthesis project, was an excellent robot configuration technician at the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, and even made his way to the secret departments of the AoC, where he truly felt his "insignificance before the vastness of the cosmos."  "I understand this world perfectly. We're all just grains of sand in an ocean of electrical connections," Comrade Petelka declared before retiring from science, effective immediately. But he did not leave the Facility. Having returned to his duties configuring robots and servicing the theater's electrical grid, Petelka is, perhaps more than any other Soviet citizen, eagerly anticipating the Kollektiv 2,0 update that will utterly efface the boundary between human cognition and the capabilities of robots.  "We're all just electric currents, just ones and zeroes" is a favorite phrase of Petelka's, who often spends his free time in the theater's coat check room observing his favorite robot, the coat check girl.

A German scientist of Jewish descent, Stockhausen worked as a doctor in Berlin during the war. He lived through the first outbreaks of the Brown Plague and was later saved by Soviet soldiers. Prior to his infection, he had an incredible memory—a fact his coworkers could attest to—but lost this ability after the onset of the illness and never demonstrated it again (although he does not regret the loss).  Thanks to his scientific and organizational talents, Stockhausen's career enjoyed a startlingly rapid ascent. He was recruited to the Facility in order to fill a quota for scientists from the German Soviet Socialist Republic and quickly earned Sechenov's respect. Despite his German pedantry and a certain degree of snobbishness, he remains one of the best-known—and best-liked—members of the Facility 3826 team. He is perfectly capable of speaking Russian without an accent, but chooses to "sound German" in order to remind people of his origins.

Comrade Lastochkin is not a traditional theater director. Better known as "Stefan," Lastochkin has had a stunning career, starting out as an office manager and becoming the head of what is perhaps the most famous theater in the world. In less than a year, unique performances such as "The Binding Screws of Friendship," "In the Vice of Passion," and the modern classic "Electric Origins" have become sensations among fans of avant-garde art. However, his narcissism, shady dealings, and despotic management style have set many theater employees at odds with the ambitious new director.

Николай Иванович Вавилов (25 ноября 1887, Москва, Российская империя) — русский и советский учёный-генетик, ботаник, селекционер, химик, географ, общественный и государственный деятель. Организатор и участник ботанико-агрономических экспедиций, охвативших большинство континентов (кроме Австралии и Антарктиды), в ходе которых выявил древние очаги формообразования культурных растений. Создал учение о мировых центрах происхождения культурных растений[6]. Обосновал учение об иммунитете растений, открыл закон гомологических рядов в наследственной изменчивости организмов. Внёс существенный вклад в разработку учения о биологическом виде. Под руководством Вавилова была создана крупнейшая в мире коллекция семян культурных растений. Он заложил основы системы государственных испытаний сортов полевых культур. Сформулировал принципы деятельности главного научного центра страны по аграрным наукам, создал сеть научных учреждений в этой области

Date: March 10, 1955 From: Vavilov Archivist D. Semushev To: Vavilov Archive Dept.  "On the Acceleration of Evolution" Despite all their talent and the indisputable success achieved by Vavilov's research assistants, there is a concern regarding an issue that, while predictable, can only be confirmed in practice. Date: January 12, 1955 From: Pavlov Complex Manager I. Pavlov To: Pavlov Cultural Archivist V. Nikitin  Progress by leaps and bounds has become typical of humanity in this challenging 20th century. Against the background of tremendous inequality, breakthroughs in science and technology can seem not just astonishing, but even insulting. But this is a sociological and political matter. Right now I want to contemplate the issue of the individual, who, feeling himself in a state of accelerated free-fall, is being flung forward faster and faster by progress. Much like the pseudo-scientific fears voiced when the railroads were being built, when the suggestion was actually made that the sight of the landscape whizzing by at 50 kilometers per hour would drive passengers mad, I am beset by similar predictions. Just 25 years ago more than half of all Soviet citizens were illiterate. Today, we are flying into space. What awaits us tomorrow? Will we have time to catch our breath before our next great leap?

Date: March 13, 1955 From: Academy of Consequences Secretary's Office To: Vavilov Archivist D. Semushev  Despite its secrecy, Argentum ("silver" in Latin) has already become the stuff of legend in a number of European and American publications. Journalists are surprised by its extremely small staff, its incredible training and equipment, and its name, which is very atypical of the Soviet Union (you've got to admit, compared to abbreviations like SMERSH and NKVD, it comes off as odd and clumsy). Rumors vary. The squad's soldiers are described either as enormous red-eyed bears who eat children or athletic blond supermen, one look at whom would have driven Hitler to dissolve the Reich and admit the German Übermensch's defeat.  They are a mystery and will remain one, but we can say this much for certain: Argentum is currently the best-trained special forces squad on Earth. And, given the Soviet Union's plans, it could become the best-trained squad in the Solar System before long.

Date: September 14, 1953 From: Publishing Dept. To: Printing Archive  "The time has come to acknowledge that we are careening into the future at an amazing speed. Our scientific machine is running at full capacity, and the most talented Soviet citizens are working day and night to advance the cause of progress. But what of evolution? The same goes for the decrepit, monarchistic phenomenon of evolution. Now man is not just the pinnacle of creation, but a creator himself, and he has the ability and the right to alter himself in accordance with his desires. Gills for divers, wings for first responders, flame-retardant skin for firemen—this is just a small sample of what awaits us in the near future. We are no longer grist for the mill of natural selection—we ARE natural selection." From Comrade Sechenov's lecture to the Soviet Academy of Sciences, 1953

Date: February 14, 1955 From: Publishing Dept. To: Printing Archive  Andrey Rayanovsky's Unknown Feat (draft of an article)  For a long time, Andrey Rayanovsky's name was spoken of with contempt and dismay in Soviet scientific circles. As a capitalist and idealist who fled the Soviet Union and a vocal critic of the Party's authority and the ideals of communism, it was obvious that a good relationship with him was simply impossible. Date: October 15, 1954 From: Pavlov Debate Club President N. Azarova to: archive terminal  Speaker: When I give talks in the Soviet Union and allied countries, I am often asked whether it makes sense to focus scientific progress on making fundamental changes to the human race. We could, for example, teach people to change the properties of their skin in order to make it more resistant to heat or cold, or regrow lost limbs like certain reptiles, or control their biochemistry on a basic level. In other words, to rephrase a well-known thesis, should we strive for "evolution in the individual?"  From the room: skeptical laughter  Speaker: My answer is "no." I admit that this is a defeatist attitude. But my objection does not lie in some bourgeois conception of man as the pinnacle of creation. We have access to powerful technology, and yet we should not alter ourselves to suit our environment. This would be a step backwards. Instead, we must perfect science in order to fully subjugate nature itself, whether it be here on Earth, or somewhere else.

Because there's no Sun! So now it's an Aldebaran flower! Think about that. And we should think about blueberries too, since they won't even be blue on Mars. We could call them "redberries," but that's no good... and "pinkberries" just sounds weird to me.

Date: March 18, 1955 From: Stenography Dept. To: ARCHIVE  Excerpt from a paper by Lebedev  In response to those who are curious about the Radio of the Future, yes, we really can listen to radio broadcasts from the future. Literally. How does it work? If you read any of my previous papers, you'll find out. But you aren't really interested in the technical details, are you? You're interested in what it can do for you. You want to know if you can buy a lottery ticket knowing that it will win, or avoid a nuclear holocaust. Am I right? It's not that simple. What we are hearing is a PROBABLE future, what could happen in ten, thirty, or fifty years based on what's happening right now. But we have never—I repeat, never—heard the same broadcast twice. A week ago the Soviet Union crumbled in 1989 and ceased to exist as a country. This morning we heard a presentation by the general secretary of the Communist Party from 1999. One day we intercepted an emergency message about the launch of nuclear missiles in 1976... I was horrified. The future DOES NOT EXIST YET. Please remember that. All we can hear is an echo of an infinite quantumized multivariance and extract the most frequently repeated tendencies from it. What we will actually see tomorrow is entirely in our hands.

Date: May 19, 1955 From: Lab Supervisor A. Privalov To: Senior Lab Assistant E. Debaltovskaya  Here's my opinion on your article "On the Culture of Instant Messaging." Date: September 21, 1954 From: Sergeant U. Baray-Ogla To: Service Settlement Manager I. Abdurakhimov   We have taken a certain M. Gorshenev, a college student and bird watcher from a Moscow State University tourist group, into custody. He was found in an unauthorized area with a guitar on his back. His hair was disheveled, and he was dressed only in his undergarments. The "bard's" testimony follows (in his own words) "Exhausted from my travels, I knocked upon the forester's door and begged lodgings for the night. An elderly man let me in, looked me over in a hospitable manner, and offered me an evening's repast. He suggested that I "make myself at home" and offered me every hospitality. Upon inquiring about my work as a folklorist, he assured me that he had many a tale to tell. As I sat at the table, it grew dark outside. The forester sat across from me, conversing at his ease. He was particularly proud to be known by all the local fauna emphasized that he enjoyed feeding the wolves. I paid this comment little mind at first, but then I heard lupine howling in the middle of the night. I was frightened, but the old fellow smiled, stood up, and left the house with nary a word. Before I could comprehend what was transpiring, he returned with a rifle, which he promptly aimed at me and sad, "My friends are hungry. Come on, pal, we're going to the forest!" I leapt out the window and fled with all possible alacrity. After a time, I was apprehended by the local constabulary." To make a long story short, our forester has been using recordings of howling wolves to play pranks on tourists again. We need to get him to stop. Student bards are one thing, but what if it was someone in the service? He'd take his rifle and shoot him in the head. Handle this.

Topic: The Atomic Heart Project Speaker: Dr. Dmitry Sechenov  Welcome, Comrades. In 1951, the capitalist imperialism of the United States, consumed by hatred and envy for the Soviet Union's magnificent scientific achievements, declared the launch of the global Energy for All program. In essence, this program is just as hypocritical as the capitalist system itself. Hiding behind a facade of lofty ideals, the capitalists strive for worldwide hegemony, the suppression of all independence other than their own, and the eradication of those who do not share their values.  At first glance, Energy for All seems incredibly noble: fifty nuclear power stations will be constructed throughout the United States in order to provide every American citizen with cheap and available electricity. But the United States' capitalist regime is, as always, hiding its true face, twisted into the beastly grin of imperialism, behind a mask of magnanimity. In addition to these power stations, the United States is also secretly building a network of underground silos and hangars for launching nuclear missiles and housing strategic bombers armed with nuclear bombs.  The Americans' goal is simple: once the Soviet Union believes their claims of peace and friendship, it will let down its guard, and the American military machine will strike, destroying the Soviet Union and the entire communist way of life with a cowardly sneak attack! But the Soviet Union isn't one to sit on its hands and wait while our enemies regroup and swell their ranks, hiding nuclear weapons underground where we cannot eliminate them from orbit. Nor is the Soviet Union one to back down or run from another nation's might. In response to the American threat, Facility 3826 has developed its own project designed not only to protect the Soviet Union, but also to rid the world once and for all of the very possibility of such a bloodbath. The president of the United States once called Energy for All America's "atomic heart." Given the profound guile and hypocrisy of American capitalism, this name reflects the essence of the global threat developed by the United States all too well. For this reason, our project, which will counteract the Americans' deadly machinations, has co-opted their leader's metaphor. Our Atomic Heart will return honestly and integrity to America!  The Atomic Heart project is made up of several sequential steps:  - Design and build civilian robots with no weapons or other signs of a potential military application. These robots have been designed to be independent of their software. Any owner can install any software onto them they like. On the outside, the robots seems to be perfectly harmless, safe, and friendly. But in reality, they are equipped with highly effective hand-to-hand combat techniques and can use civilian equipment as lethal weapons.  - Stage two of this project requires that Soviet civilian robots be seen by the entire world as humanitarian goods. We have already implemented this strategy via the United Nations. Since receiving the status of humanitarian goods, Soviet robots have begun to spread throughout the entire world free of charge, which has given a powerful impetus to the further development of the Atomic Heart project. Profit-hungry American capitalists are flooding their country with our robots. A free robotic workforce is the dream of every capitalist usurper, and none of them has hesitated to obtain as many Soviet robots as possible.  - During stage three, the Soviet Union has made obtaining free robots as easy as possible for our foreign customers. American businesses, for one, have already imported over one hundred million Soviet civilian robots of various models. Many of these are used at facilities related to Energy for All, i.e. American power stations and missile silos. There, our robots, on which American special forces have installed their own software, maintain, service, and operate nuclear facilities. The first objective of the Atomic Heart project has thus been accomplished.  - During the final phase of the project, civilian robots will be switched form civilian operation to combat mode. They will then capture all key components of the infrastructure of the United States. This will become possible with the launch of Kollektiv 2.0, which will unite all Soviet robots into a unified Neuropolymer network that requires no radio signals, digital protocols, or other electronics. All Soviet robots will be able to receive and successfully carry out our commands. Their attack will be sudden, and it will happen everywhere, all at once, down to the second. The enemy will be taken completely by surprise, and they will be eradicated. The American working class will be liberated from the oppression of global capitalism, and the very notion of capitalism will be lost in the waters of Lethe.  The launch of Kollektiv 2.0 is only two months away. In just two months, a new, progressive human race will toss capitalism into the dustbin of history, cast off the tyrants' yoke, and begin its march into the future. The world will never be the same, comrades!
Close the door on the way out

Neutron star When a star goes nova and dies, it can transform into a quickly revolving neutron star. We believe that neutron stars within a strong magnetic field could emit similar strange signals.  A merging of two stars Another potential explanation is the collision of two neutron stars. Most radio bursts detected by telescopes over the last decade have been singular.  Blitzar A quickly revolving neutron star that cannot bear its own weight, so it collapses very quickly and transforms into a black hole. Human error The imperfections inherent in available equipment (even Soviet equipment), human error when calculating data—either of these things could lead to an inaccurate interpretation.
